newsitem.title: SPAIN: FOCUS - Iraq to resume oil exports in 7-10 days.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Iraq to resume oil exports in 7-10 days.

text.p: Iraqi oil minister Amir Rasheed said on Tuesday that Iraq expected to resume exporting oil under the United Nations oil-for-food plan in the next week to 10 days after a hiatus of several weeks.

Iraq started negotiations with the U.N. last week on a distribution plan which will shortly be presented to the U.N. Secretary General, opening the way for Iraq to sell up to $2 billion of oil under the renewed oil-for-food plan, the minister said.

"We expect to start exporting oil in the next week to 10 days and we don't anticipate any problems in discussions (between the United Nations and Iraq)," Rasheed told a news conference during a trip to Spain.
The United Nations allowed Baghdad to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months ending May 30 to finance the purchase of medical and other goods. The deal has been renewed for another six months.
"We now just have to agree the distribution of money to the different areas and of course food is at the top of the list," he said.
The minister slammed suggestions that Iraq had not been cooperating with the U.N. on inspections of sensitive arms sites.

On Monday, the U.N. adopted a resolution threatening Iraq with further sanctions if it did not allow its arms inspectors full access to all sites. United Nations sanctions were imposed against Iraq in 1990 after its invasion of Kuwait.
A U.N. arms official said that while Iraq had shown readiness to cooperate with U.N. weapons inspectors, there was no indication it would allow U.N. teams full access to all sites.
As part of his trip to Madrid, Rasheed said he had continued talks with Spanish energy group Repsol SA about an exploration and development deal on the Nasiriayh oil field in central Iraq.
While an accord has yet to be concluded, the oil minister said Repsol officials would travel to Baghdad to finalise the deal but that no date had been set for the trip.

"We have exchanged views with executives from Repsol on the issues still remaining and we have agreed to continue discussions and we will have a delegation from Repsol visit Baghdad to finalise the issues which are still under consideration," Rasheed said.

Rasheed said the development of the Nasiriyah oil field would involve an investment of about $2 billion. It is also possible that Spanish companies will be involved in refining and other areas of cooperation in the country's oil sector, he said.
Repsol wants access to reserves of two billion barrels of crude in Nasiriyah oil field which represents roughly 10 percent of world oil reserves, a Repsol source said earlier.
Russia has already signed a deal with Baghdad in March to develop Iraq's Qurana oil field. Russian officials have said that no work will begin on the ground until U.N. sanctions have been lifted.
After the news conference, Rasheed left for Vienna to attend the OPEC bi-annual meeting on Wednesday.
He declined to comment on Iraq's position on OPEC output quotas.
"We will discuss this tomorrow and will make the right decision," he said.
